response: Comparisons of absolute EOA values grouped by the manufacturers' valve sizes are misleading because of specific differences in geometric dimensions. The EOA:patient aortic annulus area ratio provides a new hemodynamic index which may facilitate objective comparisons between different valve types. This ratio takes into account both the effective orifice area and patient-specific anatomical considerations, allowing for more accurate and reliable comparisons among different bioprosthetic valves. By considering these two factors together, clinicians can better evaluate the performance of each valve and make informed decisions about which one is best suited for individual patients.
